report:
test_total does not fail. It passes. The failing test is test_half_cent_rounds_up.

Test run (python -m pytest): 2 passed, 1 failed.
- test_plain: pass
- test_total: pass (399 * 0.9 = 359.1, int() gives 359, test expects 359)
- test_half_cent_rounds_up: FAIL, assert 959 == 960

Why it fails: cart.total ends with int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)).
int() cuts off the fraction, it does not round. 1010 * 0.95 = 959.5, int() gives 959,
the test expects 960 (half a cent rounds up). This is the same bug as the TODO line
"customers see totals one cent short".

Note for a fix (not made, you asked a question): plain round() will not do it, because
Python rounds 959.5 to the even number 960 but 958.5 to 958. A half up rounding in whole
cents is needed, for example with decimal ROUND_HALF_UP or integer math. Float math can
also land just under .5, so integer or Decimal math is safer.

I changed no code.
